headline: Dry, quiet weather holds through Saturday, then a coastal storm brings a soaking rain and some wind to New York City and the region Sunday into Monday, with a low-end flooding risk; another rainy coastal storm is possible around Thanksgiving but is highly uncertain.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: High pressure keeps Friday dry and quiet across New York City and the surrounding area, with light west-southwest winds under about 10 mph this afternoon. Friday night stays dry, with winds turning light from the north or northwest and going calm in many outlying areas. No watches, warnings or advisories are in effect.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Saturday stays dry, with east to southeast winds developing late in the afternoon. A coastal low-pressure system brings rain Sunday, with the storm passing through or just east of the area Sunday night into Monday; the air will be very moist, but the storm moves north quickly (about 23 mph), which limits how long the heavy rain lasts. The area is under a low-end (level 1 of 4) risk of flooding rain, and forecasters have added the potential for flooding late Sunday into Monday to their hazard outlook, though the latest trend is for slightly less rain and less wind than earlier forecasts. Rain continues early Monday with improvement likely in the afternoon and northwest-to-west gusts of about 25–30 mph, and Tuesday turns dry with weakening north-northwest winds.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Wednesday looks dry during the day, with clouds or rain possibly arriving Wednesday night. Another coastal storm could bring rain around Thanksgiving (Thursday), but the computer models disagree sharply on its track, ranging from over Cape Cod to well south of the area with strong high pressure holding over northern New England. The blended forecast puts the chance of rain around 60% for the event, mostly as rain, though some mixing with other precipitation types is possible inland at the start; if it materializes, it looks like another wind-and-rain event.

coast: Winds and seas stay below small-craft levels through Saturday. Seas on the ocean could build to 5 feet or more by the end of Sunday, and small-craft-advisory or even gale-force winds are possible on all waters Monday depending on the storm's track and strength; northwest winds behind the storm will likely reach small-craft levels Tuesday, especially on the ocean. With the full moon on Tuesday, minor coastal flooding is possible: a coastal track would push water onshore, but weaker winds may offset that, and most guidance shows little or no flooding except in the most vulnerable back-bay spots. The extreme high end of guidance touches moderate flooding at Freeport, but that is not what most guidance suggests.
watch_for: The exact track and strength of the Sunday–Monday storm, which could still shift rain totals, winds and flooding risk.
Minor flooding in vulnerable back-bay areas around high tides early next week near the full moon.
Whether a second coastal storm brings rain and wind around Thanksgiving.
confidence: Confidence has increased in a Sunday night–Monday rainstorm now that models agree, though that agreement is from only one model run so track and intensity could still change; confidence in the Thanksgiving storm is very low.
